correct_action:
persuader: Actually, many Greek refugee camps are rated as as-bad or worse than many camps in war zones. It's complete chaos, overrun by gangs and gang violence, and often lacking in basic hygiene and access to clean water or food. Women are frequently raped while trying to use the toilets (which are horrendous) and rats run amok among the tents. One of the children we were working with had a huge rat bite on her foot and many of them had fled to Greece on their own. 
persuadee: Wow!  Did you feel safe?  What could you do to help?  
persuader: It was nuts - we even had a neo-Nazi mob hunting us in the streets one night. I definitely did not feel safe there. We tried to do our best to get kids registered and provide English classes and some amount of regularity for them. Save the Children created a space just for kids and mothers and were able to assist with getting them into school
persuadee: What an amazing experience!  That kind of thing shapes your life!
distractors:
persuader: It's really incredible. The environment there is far different from what most people would imagine. We focused on providing emotional support and educational resources for the children, as many of them struggled with trauma. Establishing a stable routine made a significant difference.

persuadee: Sounds like you made a real difference. It's alarming to think about how grossly underestimated the situation can be for outsiders. What kind of impact do you think your work had on the children there?

persuader: Absolutely, collaborating with organizations like Save the Children helps bring attention to these underreported issues. It ensures that more support reaches those in need.

persuadee: That's a great point. Partnering with recognized organizations definitely amplifies the impact and helps address these critical needs more effectively.

persuader: It can be really tough working in such challenging environments, but having a strong team makes a big difference. We also try to focus on the positive impacts we can have, no matter how small.   
persuadee: That's interesting. It seems like an emotionally challenging place to work. How do you manage to handle such situations mentally?  
persuader: A good team is definitely crucial. Are there specific success stories that help keep your spirits up?  
persuadee: Absolutely! One family we assisted eventually got relocated to Germany. The kids are now attending school and thriving. It's stories like that which keep us going.

persuader: You might be surprised to know that the situation in Greek refugee camps is quite severe. How did we manage to adapt? It took some time, but the camaraderie among volunteers made a big difference. We concentrated on giving emotional support and creating safe spaces for the kids.

persuadee: I never realized it was that bad in Greece. It's incredible that you were able to offer a nurturing environment amid such chaos. How did the children react to your efforts?

persuader: They were truly inspiring! Despite all the challenges, the kids were eager to learn and showed remarkable resilience. Their spirit motivated us every single day.

persuadee: That's wonderful to hear! Creating such an environment must have been a life-changing experience for both you and the children.
